title: Dedicated capacity preflight, decommit cooling window, and emergency escalation protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a prescriptive preflight checklist, a decommit cooling window (grace period), and a clear emergency escalation protocol for Dedicated capacity reservations so customers and sales/ops teams can request, approve, change, or cancel reserved capacity with predictable economics, low operational friction, and safe autoscale overrides.

Background: Current reservation workflow accepts committed capacity without a standardized preflight validation and lacks an explicit decommit/cooling policy. This leads to frequent last-minute cancellations, revenue disputes, and production risk when customers request emergency scale-ups. We need: 1) machine-checkable preflight rules (billing/quotas/region/compatible models), 2) a defined decommit cooling window with cost/penalty schedule, 3) an emergency scaling & rollback runbook (who can approve, audit trail, fallback routing to hosted variants).

Outcomes:
- Reduced dispute events by 60% in first quarter after rollout.
- Predictable revenue recognition dates aligned with decommit windows.
- Measurable reduction in emergency manual intervention (oncall escalations) for capacity shortages.

Acceptance criteria (must be true for Done):
- Preflight automated checks implemented in the reservation UI and API that verify region capacity, model compatibility, requested throughput vs. supported pool sizing, and KMS/audit settings.
- Cooling window rules published and enforced: a 14-day standard cooling window with optional 7-day expedited window for a fee; UI shows effective earliest decommit date and cancellation cost estimate.
- Emergency escalation protocol documented and accessible from Console: steps for request, required approvals, expected time-to-fulfill, and fallback model routing policy.
- Billing/finance policy updated to reflect decommit refunds/penalties and revenue recognition mapping to effective reservation start.
- Instrumentation: dashboard tile showing outstanding cooling-window reservations, pending cancellations, emergency-scaling events, and cost exposure.

Key design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Cooling window length: 14 days chosen to balance commercial flexibility vs. capacity planning. Shorter windows increase forecast volatility; longer windows reduce customer flexibility.
- Penalty structure: tiered refunds (100% full refund before preflight sign-off window, 70% within cooling window, 0% within 48 hours of start) vs. flat fees. Tiered preferred to align incentives.
- Emergency scaling: prefer automated temporary routing to hosted-compatible variants + soft quota burst before manual hardware allocation. This reduces SLA risk but may increase per-unit cost for short periods.

Rollout plan:
1) Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement preflight checks in API only; add validation errors and helpful remediation messages.
2) Phase 2 (2 weeks): Expose cooling window dates & cost preview in Console + API; update billing ledger.
3) Phase 3 (1 week): Publish escalation runbook and add emergency-scaling button in Console for authorized roles.
4) Phase 4 (ongoing): Monitor metrics, collect feedback from Sales/CS and iterate.

Monitoring & metrics:
- KPI: reservation cancellation rate (weekly) and revenue churn from cancellations.
- KPI: number of emergency-scaling events and mean time to resolve.
- Alert: >3 emergency scaling events in 24h for same customer triggers post-incident review.

Operational notes:
- Approval matrix: Sales up to $X/month can approve expedited windows; Finance+Infra required above that threshold.
- Audit trail: every change to reservation must create an immutable event with actor, timestamp, pre/post state, and linked PR/contract.
- Compatibility: preflight must cross-check model variant compatibility (quantized vs. unquantized), required memory per request (peak_seq * batch), and any private deployment constraints (VPC endpoints, KMS key presence).
